title: Launch traffic contracts and stability fence playbook for cross-surface releases
creator: Priya Shah
description: Context: As runtime, console, and API teams coordinate increasingly frequent releases (model rollouts, kernel changes, console UX updates), we need a single operational contract that defines allowed traffic patterns, capacity hedges, and automated stability gates. Goal: produce a playbook and calendar-as-code template that product, eng, and SRE use to schedule releases in the Release Train and enforce safety fences at cutover. The artifact should include a sample traffic contract, canary thresholds, capacity reservation guidance, escalation runbook, and automation hooks for the release calendar.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical traffic contract template exists and is published in Confluence with examples for runtime/model, console, and API surface rollouts
Release calendar entries can be validated against the contract via a lint job (example GitHub Actions) that rejects entries missing required fields (capacity hedge, primary owner, canary window)
Cross-team rehearsals completed for one multi-surface release using the playbook (shadow + canary + staggered ramp) with documented metrics and at least one post-rehearsal action item list
Dashboards and alerts for the contract SLOs (p95 latency, error rate, token/sec capacity, queue depth) are linked from the release entry and tested in the rehearsal
Runbook defines clear rollback criteria and owners; at least two teams have signed off in the release entry prior to slot allocation

notes: Key decisions to capture: 1) traffic contract is a hard gate for release slot allocation; missing fields -> automatic rejection. 2) Capacity hedge formula: max(peak_estimate * 1.10, minimum_reserve) where minimum_reserve = 2 GPU equivalents for Dedicated. 3) Canary windows should be short but measurable: baseline 1 hour or 10k tokens, whichever comes first. 4) Rollback criteria: sustained >200ms increase in p95 for 3 consecutive minutes OR error-rate delta > +0.5% absolute for 5 minutes triggers immediate rollback.
